title: Repeatable enhancement of healthcare data with social determinants of health.
ehr_evidence: We requested electronic health records from the Clinical Data Repository (University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences Translational Research Institute, 2022) for all patients with chronic conditions (i.e., asthma, diabetes, heart disease, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, heart attack, and stroke), or contagious respiratory illness (i.e., influenza or COVID-19) between 2015 and 2020.
summary: Proof-of-concept study developing a repeatable process to integrate commercial consumer data with EHR to enrich social determinants of health (SDOH) factors, followed by preliminary analysis of SDOH differences between COVID-19 positive and negative patients.
key_findings: Consumer data coverage ranged from ~90% to ~54% across two vendors, with inter-compiler match rates between ~21% and 64%.

Several SDOH factors (home-ownership, marital status, presence of children, household size, economic stability indicator, and education) were significantly different between COVID-19 positive (N=1,092) and negative (N=54,330) groups (p<0.001), while estimated family-income and home market-value showed no significant difference (p=0.4 and p=0.9, respectively).
pathologies_diseases: chronic conditions (asthma, diabetes, heart disease, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, heart attack, stroke)
study_design: proof-of-concept data integration study with preliminary cross-sectional comparison
population: 55,422 patients with chronic conditions or respiratory illness (2015-2020) from a US academic medical center
limitations: restricted to only two commercial data vendors due to budget
low concordance between overlapping data elements from different vendors
data_availability_statement: The datasets presented in this article are not readily available because it contains clinical information. Requests to access the datasets should be directed to mlgreer@uams.edu.
